title: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 15 The Seven Last Plagues

sense.text: “Speak with my words unto them”: as men and women of the Lord we are to use God’s words when we teach and when we speak. That’s what we’re supposed to do.

“Behold, I have made thy face strong against their faces, and thy forehead strong against their foreheads”: we are to make our minds strong against the minds of our rebellious brothers and sisters, male and female alike. This is how I was brought up, this is how the deacons and the captains were brought up, and you brothers in the Men of Valor program are going to be built up the same way. Do y’all realize we are at war? All nations are against us. So we are going to be strong against the evil; I don’t care how much we love you, once we see you are a snake we are going to come hard against you.

“As an adamant harder than flint have I made thy forehead”: some of y’all come into this truth thinking this is church, like the Baptist church, where you can gossip and slander and it’s all good in Jesus, because you don’t believe that we are the nation of Israel. Some of you believe you are Haitians, Jamaicans or Afro-Americans, and you will die under them titles. The Lord is looking for Israelites.

“Seven angels having the seven last plagues; for in them is filled up the wrath of God”: as we discussed last week, these are seven big black terrible angels. Those of you who don’t fear the Most High read about the wrath of God and it’s like church to you; you don’t believe. When I read stuff about the wrath of God, that puts me on notice; it makes me focus on what is being said.

“A sea of glass mingled with fire”: that’s like a lake of fire, like the Lord’s throne in Daniel 7. “And them that had gotten the victory over the beast, and over his image, and over his mark, and over the number of his name”: all that represents the world. In 1 John, John makes it simple and says the world; here in Revelation he goes into more detail. This world is run by a particular race that is called the beast, and this beast has an economic system set up, a monetary buying and trade system. We must get the victory over that. Their whole banking system was founded on the backs of slaves; that is why they call it old money. Before we can deal with Esau, understand that Esau already knows there is a large majority of blacks and Latinos under their spell. The only thing that can break the spell over us is the Bible: God’s laws are the spell breaker.

precepts.why: “I beheld till the thrones were cast down”: Daniel beheld all the kingdoms on earth being destroyed. Stuff like that makes me fear when I see what is happening with so-called President Trump, the UK and the various nations, and what is going on in Haiti; it lets me know the time is near. “The Ancient of days”: because he has no beginning or end of days. “Whose garment was white as snow”: a beautiful garment. “And the hair of his head like the pure wool”: meaning God is a so-called black man. Get mad if you want; that’s what it’s saying. “His throne was like the fiery flame”: fire all around; you’re not approaching to him.

Regarding the victory. In church there was a song we used to sing, Victory is mine, and we were wicked as hell singing that song; we didn’t get no victory over nothing. “For whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world”: to be born of God means to be born again. Write that down. “And this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith.” Notice in 1 John he says victory over the world, and Revelation 15:2 is talking about the same thing. The world at that time was Rome; during these last days it is Babylon the great with all its intricate systems.

Before we get to the beast, men are called beasts. “That they might see that they themselves are beasts.” This is why a lot of people leave the Book of Revelation alone: it is written as a metaphor. You think the beast is some dangerous monster; no, it’s man.

“Having seven heads and ten horns”: seven heads meaning seven major empires: Greece, Rome, Spain, France, Germany, Russia and Britain. The ten horns are the ten common markets: Belgium, France, Germany, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Denmark, Ireland, the UK and Greece. The ten common markets are also called the EEC, the European Economic Community; they deal with finances, with money. The flip side of them is NATO, the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, their military alliance. “And upon his heads the name of blasphemy”: they go against everything the scriptures say.
This woman having a name written on her forehead represents America. “Mystery, Babylon the great, the mother of harlots and abominations of the earth.”

Remember that first beast with seven heads and ten horns: that’s the EU. “And I beheld another beast coming up out of the earth; and he had two horns like a lamb”: his two horns represent Republicanism and democracy, the two-party political group, Republicans and Democrats. Like a lamb, because the United States says In God we trust; they say this is a Christian society. “And he spake as a dragon”: meaning the things coming out of its mouth, out of their media, are really against the scriptures. For example, the Constitution says we have freedom of speech and freedom of religion; according to the scriptures you don’t have freedom of religion. How do they get us all under a spell to believe the same things? Not by a bomb, and not by business: they speak through their media. This is how they get everybody on the same page.

An example of how the Lord feels about freedom of religion. “Neither shalt thou make marriages with them”: meaning the other nations. During the 60s there was that marriage between the black woman and the white man, the Lovings, and it became so popular they said black men have gone beyond any other race marrying outside of their race. “For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods.” Let’s see if there is freedom of religion: “Ye shall destroy their altars, and break down their images, and cut down their groves, and burn their graven images with fire.” That’s thus saith the Lord; that’s against the Constitution.

“Whose deadly wound was healed”: the beast who was put to death was Rome. Rome fell around 193 AD and came back in power around 1453, the Renaissance. The word renaissance means rebirth; they were reborn in the earth again. This is why many of America’s holidays are based upon ancient Rome. “So that he maketh fire come down from heaven on the earth in the sight of men”: America was the first of these European nations to create the atom bomb; they dropped two bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki. That bomb was so powerful it made them that were near the center of the explosion into ash.

“That they should make an image to the beast”: this image came from ancient Rome. The image which symbolized him in terms of worship was none other than Caesar B…, the second son of Pope Alexander VI of Rome. His image was used to personify the Renaissance image of Jesus Christ. “And he had power to give life unto the image of the beast”: they gave that image the life of Christ, and this was orchestrated from Rome, what we call the Vatican City today. “That the image of the beast should both speak”: they have this image speak in their media; they find actors that resemble him, like that play Jesus Christ Superstar. They had him like a damn sodomite dancing around Central Park. “And cause that as many as would not worship the image of the beast should be killed”: whoever would not worship that image as Christ was killed. They did that to the North American Indians, the so-called Mexicans, Puerto Ricans and Dominicans, and to the slaves when they came over from the West Coast of Africa. That’s history.

“Both small and great, rich and poor, free and bond”: small nations and great nations, rich nations and poor nations, free nations and third world countries. “To receive a mark in their right hand, or in their foreheads”: the right hand means you support it; the forehead means you believe it. Some of you run around talking about a computer chip; go tell the Arabs or Russia they must put a computer chip in their hand and see what Putin does. I’m not saying they are not trying to make one, but to get all the people on the earth to obey that is impossible. “That no man might buy or sell”: now he is getting specific. The more modern terms for buying and selling are trade and commerce, or traffick: business deals.

I gave this last week. “And through his policy”: that’s the word I wanted; it is a more modern word than mark. When you think of the word mark you think of a tattoo; it’s not talking about a tattoo on your forehead, it’s talking about policies that you support and policies that you believe in. “And by peace shall destroy many”: when America sends their policies throughout the world, that is how they destroy countries.

Sometimes scriptures is bigger than the world of the Negro. The world of the Negro, all we know is right here, my little hood, that's all I know. The Bible's going outside of the realm of the ghetto. What are they buying and selling? Now you tell me if this is the Negro or not. “And the merchants of the earth”: that's not an ordinary word that Negroes use. A more modern word for merchants is corporations, companies; this is big business, world dominance. This is why they set up the Panama Canal and the Suez Canal, to cut the time ships take transporting goods. “The merchandise of gold, and silver, and precious stones”: a lot of these things they get from Africa; ivory comes from elephants in Africa. “And slaves, and souls of men”: part of the merchandise being bought and sold is slaves. Like the great deacon said, on a ship you have merchandise where the cargo would normally go; when it came to slaves, we were the cargo. Our fathers, our mothers, our sons and our daughters were the merchandise.

“By thy traffick”: traffick means business, buying and selling. “Hast thou increased thy riches, and thine heart is lifted up because of thy riches.” This chapter also goes into the beast, which is America, and how wealthy they are; it calls it the prince of Tyrus. It’s a metaphor, but it is talking about the same thing.

“Count the number of the beast: for it is the number of a man”: 666. The first six represents the sixth seal, the second six represents the sixth trumpet and the third six represents the sixth vial; you can read about the sixth seal in Revelation 6:12 and the sixth trumpet in Revelation 9:13-14. It all talks about the destruction of a particular race. They are the 666; that’s their number, it symbolizes them and nobody else.

“The wellfavoured harlot”: that’s Babylon the great. “The mistress of witchcrafts, that selleth nations through her whoredoms”: that lets you know it is what we just read about. I’m not talking about voodoo; how does the white man put people under a spell so everybody says the same thing, like color doesn’t matter?
“Thou hast multiplied thy merchants above the stars of heaven”: that’s all about the corporations, the companies.

“For thy merchants were the great men of the earth”: the corporations. “For by thy sorceries were all nations deceived”: that’s it right there. Their sorceries begin with their media. Last week we showed the video where all the news networks kept saying the same thing, this is a very difficult time for our democracy, and now our people are saying it too. Even in Cuba, which had nothing to do with American money, they had ABC and NBC playing in the hotel, and the people on the street in Spanish were saying the same dumb things people in America say, like Jesus has no color. Where are they getting this from? The media, TV.

sense.text: “And they sing the song of Moses the servant of God”: what do most churches say? That the Old Testament is done away with. Then why are the saints, the 144,000 and the great multitude, singing the song of Moses? Because it plays a pivotal part historically. So now we understand what the song of Moses is about: the Lord delivers us out of Egypt, we became fat under Solomon, we rejected the Lord of heaven and earth, we went into slavery and captivity, death and destruction, and then at the end the Lord brings judgment on the nations for what they did to us. That’s it in a nutshell. “And the song of the Lamb”: Christ dying on the cross for us, that messenger who did not judge based upon his sight or his ears; he magnified the law and made it honourable. Both songs are about us being redeemed and put back on top as the top nation.

precepts.why: “Write ye this song for you, and teach it the children of Israel”: we are the children of Israel; we got to learn this song. “That this song may be a witness for me against the children of Israel.” “That floweth with milk and honey”: to have milk you need cows, to feed the cows you need grass, and honey comes from bees that get it from flowers. This is talking about a rich vegetative land; that’s what the promised land was and will be again. “And waxen fat”: it does not mean we became fat slobs; it means rich. When the Israelites get rich they are going to turn against him. “For it shall not be forgotten out of the mouths of their seed”: he doesn’t want the children of the Israelites to forget this song.

“While I am yet alive with you this day, ye have been rebellious against the Lord; and how much more after my death?” “And evil will befall you in the latter days”: notice Moses is talking about even the latter days.

Ezra tells us what Moses saw, in brief. “Where I held him by me a long season”: that long season was 40 days and 40 nights. “And shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end”: Christians say God gave Moses Ten Commandments in 40 days and 40 nights; does it take 40 days to give Ten Commandments? Moses saw from Genesis all the way to the second coming of Christ. That’s why when God told Moses he was not getting into the land, Moses didn’t bug out: he saw his resurrection; he saw it all. So Moses is going to tell us everything right now in this song.

Deuteronomy 31:19-22 gave you a brief synopsis of the song; chapter 32 goes into more detail. “My doctrine shall drop as the rain, my speech shall distil as the dew”: Moses is teaching us a song that God’s law will cover the whole earth; everything is going to be wet with God’s word.
What is God’s doctrine? “For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law.” The law is his doctrine. What is the true religion? The law. What is the true doctrine? The law.
Regarding the rock. “The God of my rock; in him will I trust.” The Lord our God is the Rock.

“He is the Rock, his work is perfect.” “They have corrupted themselves, their spot is not the spot of his children”: referring to us. God gave us the laws to walk upright and we went into sin; we rebelled. “O foolish people and unwise”: notice it is calling us foolish and unwise. “Ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee”: the father and the elders are similar. “When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance”: God never intended for nations to be together; at the tower of Babel all people came together and God said that is not good, but America says we are going to bring all nations together under us. That’s the name of blasphemy. “He set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel”: he gave the Israelites the best allotment of land and based upon that gave other nations their land. “Jacob is the lot of his inheritance”: we’re his favorite. “He found him in a desert land”: the desert land was Egypt, and the wilderness was the 40 years going around; he instructed us, he gave us laws. “He kept him as the apple of his eye”: meaning his love. “He made him to suck honey out of the rock”: God blessed us wherever we went.

Write this down: the word Jeshurun means upright ones. This is another name for the Israelites; we are the upright ones, because he gave us his laws and made a covenant with us. “But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked”: when did we wax fat? The pinnacle of our kingdom was under Solomon. “Then he forsook God which made him”: after Solomon died the kingdom got split under Rehoboam and Jeroboam. Under Solomon’s reign we were glorious, and it shall be so again under Christ.

“And the sitting of his servants”: everything was done in order; the servants sat down at a particular time, in a particular way. We have not learned that yet. “And their apparel”: she made note of the clothes they wore; they were not dressed like servants. “And his cupbearers”: the way they brought the drink and the way the cup was decorated. “And his ascent by which he went up unto the house of the Lord”: the way he walked up; there was probably music playing. “There was no more spirit in her”: she was blown away.
“So king Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth for riches and for wisdom.”
“The rock of our salvation.” That’s what Moses said: when y’all wax fat and are wealthy beyond belief, you are going to forsake the Lord, and that’s exactly what happened.
Paul made it crystal clear: “And that Rock was Christ.” That rock we were dealing with under Moses was Christ, so don’t let nobody tell you Christ is not in the Old Testament.

“They provoked him to jealousy with strange gods”: Jeroboam set up false gods for the Israelites to worship and made priests of the lowest of the people. Moses saw it way before it happened because God showed it to him. “To new gods that came newly up”: we often use this precept for today. Islam is a new god that came 600 years after Christ walked the earth, and that image of white Jesus is new; that’s the Renaissance image. “Of the Rock that begat thee thou art unmindful”: what was true back then is true for today.

How far our people the Israelites have gone. “In the last days”: the last days are today’s days. “Lovers of their own selves”: when you hear somebody say me, me, me, that’s a lover of self. “Covetous”: give me, pay me. “Unthankful”: before we came into this truth we were all grimy, but when the Lord brought men into our lives to teach us who we are, some of us became unthankful. “Without natural affection”: you thought brothers and sisters were your friends, but money was the friend. “Lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God”: money is good, but when it becomes your god there is a problem. “Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof”: they learned the scriptures, but what the law says, they reject. “From such turn away”: when you meet men and women like that, leave them alone. Clear out your Facebook friends and start again.

What does the Bible say pride is? “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.” If you have a problem with your brother, the law says go to your brother; when someone says I’m not doing what the Bible says, I have another way, that’s pride. “For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that hath it shall pour out abomination”: listen to the evil that comes out of the men and women who have pride: pay me, give me my business, you don’t have to keep the Passover anymore.

There is nothing worse than a covetous man. “Why is earth and ashes proud?” Earth and ashes is us, mankind. “There is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man: for such an one setteth his own soul to sale”: you will sell your own soul when you’re covetous. “Because while he liveth he casteth away his bowels”: you will give up your body for what you want, for fame or money.

The Lord told us he would hide his face from us. “Then shall they cry unto the Lord, but he will not hear them: he will even hide his face from them at that time, as they have behaved themselves ill in their doings.” When he hides his face he is not hearing our prayers.

“I will hide my face from them, I will see what their end shall be: for they are a very froward generation, children in whom is no faith.” Froward means habitually disposed to disobedience and opposition. When the Lord says from such turn away and a sister or a brother says I’m not doing it, they are froward. No faith, because he is telling you what is going to happen if you don’t obey, and you do it anyway: the captivity and all these things happened to us because we lost faith.

This verse is heavy. “And I will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people; I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation.” Who is Moses talking about? After Solomon the kingdom was split and the northern kingdom went into idolatry; they were considered not a people.

Verses 9 and 10 go together. The chosen generation, the royal priesthood, the holy nation is Israel. “Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God”: the northern kingdom was called Gentiles. This is what Peter is revealing that Moses prophesied would happen.
“Will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?” The dispersed are the scattered Israelites; they called the scattered Israelites Gentiles. They were not a people.

“First Moses saith, I will provoke you to jealousy by them that are no people”: Paul is reminding us about the song of Moses, which you were supposed to tell your children’s children. “I was found of them that sought me not”: those were the Gentile Israelites in idolatry, worshipping wood and stone; the apostles went to them and said you’re the Israelites, repent, and they started to change their lives. “But to Israel he saith”: to the Israelites that knew the law and the commandments, “All day long I have stretched forth my hands unto a disobedient and gainsaying people.”
“They shall be burnt with hunger, and devoured with burning heat”: that happened during the time of Babylon. “I will also send the teeth of beasts upon them”: animals turned on us.

“I will also send wild beasts among you, which shall rob you of your children”: you can see that historically in the Roman coliseums, and in the movie Django they showed them sicking dogs on us. During slavery they would take a black woman’s baby, tie a string around it and leave it on the shore for an alligator, gator bait, then pull the alligator to shore and make belts, shoes and purses out of its skin.

“The sword without, and terror within, shall destroy both the young man and the virgin, the suckling also with the man of gray hairs”: they didn’t care how young or how old you were. “I said, I would scatter them into corners”: we were scattered throughout the earth from nation to nation.

“That the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.” This is why no matter where the diaspora is, we don’t remember that we’re the Israelites. It’s prophecy; for you not to believe the Bible, you’re insane. We are living it and don’t even realize it.

“Lest they should say, Our hand is high, and the Lord hath not done all this”: the nations which destroyed us gave honour to themselves; they didn’t say the Lord allowed this, they said we did this. “O that they were wise, that they understood this, that they would consider their latter end!” “How should one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, except their Rock had sold them”: one enemy chased a thousand of us because our God had sold us.
“And the sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them; and they shall flee, as fleeing from a sword.” The Lord took that brave, fearless spirit we once had.

“For their rock is not as our Rock, even our enemies themselves being judges”: our enemies, being judges over us, worship a strange god. “Their wine is the poison of dragons”: everything that comes out of the mouth of the nations which are our enemies.

“Their poison is like the poison of a serpent”: whatever doctrines they come with. “They are like the deaf adder that stoppeth her ear”: you telling them about injustice or reparations, or trying to reform them with your clever words, it falls on deaf ears. Another gunman just killed people in Illinois, and our people say they need more training; no, the Bible says they are like the deaf snake.
“Is not this laid up in store with me, and sealed up among my treasures?” Moses is saying the wisdom of the Lord is found in his book, his writings.

“And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times”: that will make you stable in life. “The fear of the Lord is his treasure”: his treasure is the holy scriptures. When you see men and women unstable in life, they are not following the laws of the Bible at all.

“When he seeth that their power is gone, and there is none shut up, or left”: we have no political power, no economic power, no military power in the earth; all the black leaders that rose up, they assassinated. “Where are their gods, their rock in whom they trusted”: Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. worshipped white Jesus; where was his god? Malcolm X was assassinated; where was his god? The Most High had them taken out, and he is forcing us to return to him as the Israelites. “Neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand”: once the Most High puts a judgment on us no man can undo it; we have to abide the time till the Lord says enough is enough.

“If I whet my glittering sword”: whet means to sharpen. “And will reward them that hate me”: that is talking about wicked Israelites, many of whom know that they are Israelites. He says you hate me; I’m going to kill you too.
“For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea”: that’s the enemy. “And upon the people of my curse, to judgment.”

“But he that sinneth against me wrongeth his own soul”: you think you are hurting us by not doing what the Bible says; you are hurting your own soul. “All they that hate me love death”: our people that reject the commandments of God.

“The prophet is a fool, the spiritual man is mad”: because they are going against God’s laws. “For the multitude of thine iniquity, and the great hatred”: who says our people don’t hate God? When judgment or a test comes on them you’ll see men and women turn and hate God, and they will never say it; they say it’s because of you.
“But his citizens hated him”: his citizens, the Israelites. “We will not have this man to reign over us”: we don’t want Christ to be our king.

This is for those that hate the Lord. “But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me.” Nobody says out of their mouth I hate the Lord, but it shows in their actions. In the wilderness our forefathers never said we hate the Lord; they said we don’t like you Moses, we don’t like you Aaron. But the Lord said to Moses they are not mad at you; it is really against me. The same is true today.
“I will make mine arrows drunk with blood”: that’s missiles, destruction.
“For by fire and by his sword will the Lord plead with all flesh: and the slain of the Lord shall be many.” This is why we don’t have time to play games; we are very serious about this Bible.

“Rejoice, O ye nations, with his people”: the nations are going to praise us; some nations are going to honour us. “And will be merciful unto his land, and to his people”: he is not being merciful on all nations, only on his people, the Israelites. “He, and Hoshea the son of Nun”: Hoshea is Joshua.

This is how the nations are going to praise us. “Every one that is left of all the nations”: all the nations that are not destroyed by Christ and the Israelites. “Shall even go up from year to year to worship the King”: they are going to be forced to go up and keep the high holy days. “Even upon them shall be no rain”: that means famine, death; that’s the judgment. “If the family of Egypt go not up”: that is the real Egyptians, not the Arabs you got there today.
What is the song of the Lamb? “Behold my servant, whom I uphold”: that’s Christ. “He shall bring forth judgment to the Gentiles.”

“Sing unto the Lord a new song.” “The villages that Kedar doth inhabit”: Kedar means dark-skinned, talking about the Arab families. “Let the inhabitants of the rock sing”: we are the inhabitants of the Lord. Now here is the song of the Lamb: “The Lord shall go forth as a mighty man”; “I will destroy and devour at once.” Christ is going to do a whole lot of killing when he returns. “I will make waste mountains and hills”: big governments and little governments. “And I will bring the blind by a way that they knew not”: we’re the blind, because we couldn’t see what the scriptures were saying. “I will make darkness light before them”: everything so unclear to us he is going to make clear. “And not forsake them”: Christ is not going to forsake us. “They shall be turned back, they shall be greatly ashamed, that trust in graven images”: the nations. “Who is blind, but my servant? or deaf, as my messenger that I sent?”: when the Lord sends the messengers, they don’t judge according to their eyes or their ears. “He will magnify the law, and make it honourable”: it must be the same way amongst us; I don’t care how well you like somebody, what does the law say?

“Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment.” Go by what the Bible says. When you go by your eyes you go, that’s my friend, I like him; that’s my sister, I love her. Many of those that fell out of this congregation judged according to appearance. Righteous judgment means what does the law say: go to your brother or sister one on one, not social media.

“Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them”: the idols that you created. People use this to say you shouldn't have graven images, but they don't read the whole thing. The issue of graven images is when you bow down to them. Bow down to them is a form of worship. When you create graven images and you worship it, God doesn't like that.

“For I the Lord thy God am a jealous God”: how is God a jealous God? “Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me.” You can't knock on God's door and tell him you hate him. It explains here that when you hate him, it's in your actions. Like during the time of the wilderness, our forefathers never said "I hate the Lord" out of their mouth, but in their actions, like when they murmured against Moses, it was really against the Lord.

“Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone”: if I got a problem with a brother, should I go to someone else about it? No. The Bible says you go to your brother, you go to your sister. But instead, people go on Facebook, they go on YouTube, evil as hell.

Why did Christ have to put that in the Bible? Why did the Son of God have to make it a law? Because we still have that same spirit Christ was trying to stop back then. It should be basic common knowledge, but he knew it was going to happen, so he had it written and documented.

sense.text: “For all nations shall come and worship before thee”: that goes back to Zechariah 14:16; the nation that will not serve the King shall die. Not only are we going to be the top nation, we got a job to do: to force the nations to worship the one true God, because they are not going to do it willingly. “For thy judgments are made manifest”: this is what the world doesn’t want; they don’t want God’s judgments to be made manifest. We do, because God is a God of justice, and the black man has never seen justice in the earth.

precepts.why: “For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish.” “And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee”: they are going to be our slaves. “For in my wrath I smote thee”: he made us slaves. “But in my favour have I had mercy on thee”: he is going to set us on top as the top nation on earth. “That men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles”: the wealth of the nations. “The sons also of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee”: Esau loves to ask, do you think it’s right that the children pay for the sins of the fathers? Yes, because there is such a thing as regeneration; you are your fathers come back. “Thou shalt also suck the milk of the Gentiles”: everything the Gentiles got belongs to us. “For brass I will bring gold, and for iron I will bring silver.” “I will also make thy officers peace, and thine exactors righteousness”: thine exactors, your tax collectors. When our kingdom is set up the nations are going to bring taxes to us; as long as we got to pay tax to another race we ain’t free.

Somebody said there is not supposed to be no rank in Israel. “And ordain elders in every city”: there must be rank; somebody has to play the role of elders. It is always leadership; people never just do whatever they want. What Bible are they reading?
Some of y’all think when Christ comes back everybody is going to be happy and praise him; that’s a lie. “And they repented not to give him glory”: the nations are not going to submit.

“And I will lay my vengeance upon Edom by the hand of my people Israel.” People say vengeance is the Lord’s; yes, vengeance is the Lord’s, and he is going to let the Israelites get vengeance. Give your church pastor that.

“And the nations were angry”: they are going to be angry when the Lord returns. “And that thou shouldest give reward unto thy servants the prophets, and to the saints, and them that fear thy name, small and great”: the reward is power, to the Israelites, the smallest among us to the greatest. “And shouldest destroy them which destroy the earth”: with his pollutions, his chemicals, his biological warfare and his nuclear wars.

Revelation uses the word reward; here it says judgment. “And judgment was given to the saints of the most High”: what judgment is going to be given to us? Power, being changed in the twinkling of an eye.

“But the saints of the most High shall take the kingdom”: we ain't asking for a damn thing we going to take it. This is why it behooves every man and every woman to stay in line with the laws of God and not be sidetracked with evil. There is a great reward for each one of us.

sense.text: “And the seven angels came out of the temple”: the seven black angels. Your grandmama has little white angels on the wall with yellow hair, butt naked with a bow and arrow; that’s not in the Bible. “Clothed in pure and white linen”: their garments were decked out; these were not Greek togas. The Israelites that followed the laws did not dress like Greeks. As we went over last week, the temple built by King Solomon is based upon the temple in heaven; everything is based upon the pattern of the heavens. “And having their breasts girded with golden girdles”: big wrestling belts, gold with studs.
“And one of the four beasts gave unto the seven angels seven golden vials full of the wrath of God”: the four beasts are the terrible archangels, more terrible than these seven.

“Till the seven plagues of the seven angels were fulfilled”: these seven plagues are the judgments of war coming upon the earth, which lead up to the great river Euphrates being dried up, World War III commencing and Christ’s return.

precepts.why: To show that they are black. “Their appearance was like burning coals of fire”: a coal is black. So the angels are not Caucasian, and they don’t have yellow stringy hair.
We read it last week. “His countenance was like the countenance of an angel of God, very terrible”: when you think the angels are cute and loving, you’ve been bewitched by America’s media, by Esau.

sense.text:
“Be ashamed of whoredom before father and mother: and of a lie before a prince and a mighty man”: the Bible says to be ashamed of that. In the Apocrypha, where it lists the things to be ashamed of. In some things you can be shamefaced, but in these things you must be ashamed.

“Of an offence before a judge and ruler; of iniquity before a congregation and people; of unjust dealing before thy partner and friend”: and of theft in regard of the place where thou sojournest, and in regard of the truth of God and his covenant. And to lean with thine elbow upon the meat, and of scorning to give and take, and of silence before them that salute thee.

“For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock”: that's what he is, he is a grievous wolf. You ever see a wolf when it's attacking? A pack of wolves won't let the animal go; the animal will be trying to run away limping and everything, they'll follow it. That's why they call them grievous wolves, they cause grief.

“Not sparing the flock”: they don't care about the congregation. His agenda is not to teach you, it's to reach you so he could use you as merchandise and make money off of you. “Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them.”

“O that they were wise, that they understood this, that they would consider their latter end!”: Moses wants you to know that no matter what captivity you're in, be wise keeping God's commandments. Consider your latter end, meaning keep God's commandments no matter what, no matter what you're going through.

We read about Jonah in the land of Nineveh, God eyes was on the brother. We read about Jeremiah when the princes kept putting him in the dungeon, guess what, God was with him. That's what's going to help us in this captivity, us keeping God's commandments. God will open doors for us.

“And the fifth angel poured out his vial upon the seat of the beast; and his kingdom was full of darkness; and they gnawed their tongues for pain”: a lot of us must be saying "I don't know why he's saying that." I believe what this Bible says. Watch this.

“And blasphemed the God of heaven because of their pains and their sores, and repented not of their deeds.”

“If any man speak in an unknown tongue, let it be by two, or at the most by three, and that by course; and let one interpret”: if you're speaking around other people, they should not be looking at you wondering what you are saying. That is evil, that's what the Bible says.

There's a law that you're not supposed to come up here speaking Spanish around other people and they don't know what you're saying. You're not supposed to come here speaking no Spanish, no Haitian Creole, around other people. The scriptures tell you because they have the advantage with another language, just sitting in the congregation having one-on-one conversations.
